title: LowGradQ: Adaptive Gradient Quantization for Low-Bit CNN Training via Kernel Density Estimation-Guided Thresholding and Hardware-Efficient Stochastic Rounding Unit
problem: On-device CNN training requires low-bit precision but stochastic rounding in INT8 training imposes high computational and memory overhead; generating quality random numbers for rounding is a bottleneck.
motivation: On-device training is emerging as critical for IoT and edge deployment, requiring hardware-efficient gradient handling that minimizes entropy generation and rounding complexity.
method: Proposes dual-scale adaptive gradient quantization (DAGQ) capturing both small and large-magnitude gradients with kernel density estimation-guided thresholding; introduces LFSR-based reusable stochastic rounding unit (RLSRU) that generates and reuses random numbers efficiently, reducing hardware complexity.
key_novelty: LFSR-based reusable stochastic rounding unit eliminating redundant random number generation in low-bit training.
contributions: Dual-scale adaptive gradient quantization capturing gradient magnitude range
Kernel density estimation-guided thresholding for optimal quantization boundaries
LFSR-based reusable stochastic rounding unit reducing random number generation overhead
Stable INT8 training across diverse networks with minimal accuracy loss
limitations: Specific accuracy degradation percentages and speedup metrics not provided; evaluation limited to CNN training.
